summary: Iteration 7 - Verified new features: (a) principal helper 'Aidé par' per-ticket, (b) Gemini French summary via Emergent LLM key with structured JSON keys, (c) admin-only overview panel gated by Discord role 1503100661728936046. Added /app/backend/tests/test_admin_and_ai_summary.py (36 tests, all pass) plus fixed 2 stale assertions in test_iris_api.py and test_demo_removed.py made obsolete by the RBAC refactor (has_iris_access now unifies helper+admin gates and session re-derivation now happens on every /auth/session read). Full pytest run against public preview URL: 82/82 pass. Playwright pass against https://iris-logs.preview.emergentagent.com desktop 1920x1080 + mobile 390x844: LoginPage renders discord-login-button, and neither admin-panel-link, admin-dashboard-page, helper-assignment-panel, ai-summary-panel nor any demo-access element renders while unauthenticated. Visiting /admin without a session redirects to LoginPage (React SPA route guard). Backend-side we confirmed: GET /api/admin/overview, GET /api/admin/helpers, PATCH /api/admin/tickets/{id}/assignment and POST /api/tickets/{id}/ai-summary/stream all return 401 without a session; a HMAC-signed mode=discord cookie for a fabricated user id (18-digit snowflake that does not exist on the guild) is refused by /admin/overview (never returns admin data). Live OAuth callback + real Gemini call against a real ticket were intentionally NOT executed (needs a human Discord admin account, per review request).
action_items: HUMAN VERIFICATION: a real Discord account holding role 1503100661728936046 must complete the OAuth handshake once to (a) confirm session.is_admin=true in /api/auth/session, (b) confirm the sidebar admin-panel-link appears and /admin renders the AdminDashboardPage populated by DiscordService.fetch_helpers, (c) trigger POST /api/tickets/{id}/ai-summary/stream on a real ticket to confirm Gemini actually returns a valid JSON object parseable by parse_summary, and (d) run PATCH /api/admin/tickets/{id}/assignment with a real helper_id to confirm 422 is returned when an unauthorized helper_id is supplied. Automation cannot cover this without touching production Discord and Gemini quota.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/admin.py:admin_overview - iterates the full ticket list once per helper (O(H*T)). Fine for the current scale (250-ticket cap, small helper roster) but if the roster grows past a few hundred and tickets stay at 250, consider indexing tickets by assigned_helper.id first. Not blocking.

routers/admin.py:assign_ticket_helper - correctly re-fetches the authorized helper list from Discord and stores HelperIdentity.model_dump() (server-derived) instead of the raw client payload. The client never controls display_name/avatar_url of the stored assignment. Good.

routers/auth.py:/session - now calls has_iris_access(helper.id) on every session read; when Discord returns 404 for a stale user the underlying DiscordService raises HTTPException(404) which bubbles all the way up as a 404 response instead of returning {authenticated:false,is_admin:false}. Frontend App.js catches this via .catch() -> setSession({authenticated:false}) so UX is fine, but it would be cleaner to catch HTTPException inside the session endpoint and return the unauthenticated shape explicitly. Not a security issue, minor UX/observability polish.

services/ai_summary_service.py:parse_summary - if Gemini returns a JSON array (permitted by the prompt: 'phrase ou liste courte') the isinstance(str) check falls back to 'Non précisé dans le dossier.' silently. Consider stringifying list values or extending the aliases to accept list/tuple, otherwise valid Gemini responses that use short bullet lists will be replaced by the fallback string. Low priority, but likely to surprise E1 during live tests.

services/ai_summary_service.py - .with_model('gemini', 'gemini-3.5-flash') pins the model string exactly as the user requested. Emergent LLM key is server-side only; no frontend file references EMERGENT_LLM_KEY. Verified.

services/discord_service.py:fetch_helpers - uses limit=1000 (Discord API max is 1000 for GET /guilds/{guild}/members), paginates with `after` on the last member's user.id, and exits when the page is short. Correct. Note this route requires the GUILD_MEMBERS privileged intent to be enabled on the bot; if it isn't, the endpoint 403s and the admin overview will surface 'Le bot ne peut pas accéder à cette ressource Discord.' Verify that intent is enabled during human OAuth verification.

models/ticket.py:TicketAssignmentUpdate.helper_id - pattern locks the input to a Discord snowflake (15-22 digits). Combined with the fetch_helpers whitelist check in the router, this makes helper impersonation via freeform client input impossible.

frontend/TicketWorkspacePage.jsx - the helper-assignment-select is conditionally rendered from isAdmin; non-admins see a read-only 'Non attribué' label. isAdmin flows from session.is_admin down through App.js -> AuthenticatedApp -> TicketWorkspacePage. Verified.

components/AppShell.jsx - the admin-panel-link NavLink is wrapped in {isAdmin && ...}. If a compromised client tampered with isAdmin in local state, the /admin route would render AdminDashboardPage which immediately calls /api/admin/overview and gets 403 from current_admin. Client-side gating is UX-only; RBAC is server-derived on every request. Correct defense-in-depth.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_demo_removed.py (updated test_signed_discord_mode_session_is_accepted_by_session_endpoint to reflect iteration-7 session re-derivation via Discord)

success_rate.frontend: 100% Playwright static checks on desktop 1920x1080 + mobile 390x844. Live OAuth + real Gemini generation not automated.

test_credentials: None. /app/memory/test_credentials.md is empty (Discord OAuth + Discord admin role assignment require live human accounts, per review request).
seed_data_creation: None. Admin overview / assignment / AI-summary flows were exercised only via auth-guard tests (401) and static contract tests. No production data written.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite is now 3 files: test_iris_api.py (34 tests, OAuth + guild/role invariants), test_demo_removed.py (12 tests, demo removal invariants) and test_admin_and_ai_summary.py (36 tests, admin RBAC + Gemini contract + SSE headers + frontend static invariants for helper-assignment-panel/ai-summary-panel/admin-dashboard-page). Run with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview> pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v`. If the AI-summary system prompt is edited, TestGeminiServiceContract will fire. If the admin router is changed to accept a helper session instead of admin, TestAdminRbacServerSide will fire. The only untested surface is: (a) live Gemini generation persisting a real ai_summary on a real ticket, and (b) the actual admin badge lighting up in the UI after Discord OAuth — both need a human admin login.
rca of the issue: Not a bug fix - feature validation. Iteration 7 verifies that E1 correctly added (1) an admin-only endpoint surface (/api/admin/{helpers,overview,tickets/{id}/assignment}) protected by current_admin (which re-derives the admin role from Discord role ID 1503100661728936046 on every call, so an authenticated helper cannot access it via cookie tampering), (2) a Gemini streaming SSE endpoint (/api/tickets/{id}/ai-summary/stream) that produces the four French-labelled fields context/expressed_needs/actions/next_follow_up using gemini-3.5-flash via the server-side Emergent LLM key, and (3) an AdminDashboardPage plus a conditional admin-panel-link in AppShell. The two pre-existing pytest failures were caused by stale assertions that predated the has_iris_access unification and the session re-derivation — they were fixed to reflect the new behavior, not by weakening the security checks. Demo mode remains fully absent.
